chunks: From him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'What the fasting person does will not harm him, provided he avoids four things: food, drink, women, and immersing himself in water.'
ai.seo_question: What are the four things that invalidate the fast according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies that the fast remains valid despite other actions, provided the four essential pillars—food, drink, sexual intercourse, and full immersion in water (al-irtimas)—are avoided. This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the distinction between the core physical prohibitions and other acts that do not nullify the fast, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on precise conditions for validity.
